claims.text: A 20 nm compositionally graded transition layer from CoCrFeNi to W can be inserted into an HEA multilayer.
The CoCrFeNi-to-W graded layer will produce a controlled evolution of interface coherency.
The controlled evolution of interface coherency will shift the dominant creep mechanism from diffusion-mediated creep to dislocation-mediated creep.
The initial CoCrFeNi HEA multilayers have sharp or uniformly coherent interfaces.
Dual-target sputtering with programmatically varied composition can create the proposed CoCrFeNi-to-W graded layer.
Annealing the graded multilayer at 550°C for 1 hour is an appropriate post-deposition treatment for producing the proposed effect.
A gradual change in lattice parameters across the transition layer minimizes abrupt misfit strain.
A gradual change in lattice parameters permits a continuous evolution of interface coherency.
The graded layer reduces local lattice misfit at the interface.
The graded layer reduces interfacial stress concentrations.
The resulting stress distribution and defect arrangement favor dislocation nucleation and glide over atomic diffusion.
The graded transition layer will reduce indicators of diffusion-mediated creep.
The graded transition layer will increase indicators of dislocation-mediated creep.
The creep-mechanism shift will be detectable through changes in creep rate, dislocation density, and microstructure.
HEA multilayers with sharp interfaces and no graded layer are expected to exhibit predominantly diffusion-mediated creep under the same high-temperature conditions.
The proposed phenomenon should be observable near 550°C under creep stresses relevant to high-temperature coating applications.
The effect is expected to apply to multilayers similar in composition and structural design to the proposed CoCrFeNi/W system.
